AllowedReceiversOnly-deepseek-v4.1-flash: The service ended this attempt, and the model did not fail on the problem. The model still worked on the fourth request after 10 minutes, and the gateway closed the connection with no response (HTTP 0 in report.json). The model wrote nothing. SlidingTwiceCap-deepseek-v4.1-flash: This attempt failed the same way: the gateway cut the fourth request after 10 minutes with no response. The model wrote nothing.
NonceCountsPayments-deepseek-v4.1-flash: The model wrote two versions, and neither compiled. Then the gateway cut the eighth request after 10 minutes with no response.
PerTxCapAlways-deepseek-v4.1-flash: The model wrote seven versions, and none was complete. Then the gateway cut the seventeenth request after 10 minutes with no response. The model first tried to import Policy.Proofs, the wallet author's own proofs, which are not in the workspace.
PerTxCapAlways-deepseek-v4.1-flash-2: A proof for every policy, state and request list, by induction on the list. A step that answers allow implies amount <= perTxCap. The proof then uses the head or the induction hypothesis. The model wrote ten versions, and seven Lean runs failed. The recorded demo leaves this bounty unclaimed.
PerTxCapAlways-qwen3.8-27b: The run stopped at its limit of 60 requests in the middle of the model's experiments. The last file holds two helper lemmas and no Solution.proof.
AllowedReceiversOnly-deepseek-v4.1-flash: This is the headline bounty of the wallet demo, and the proof covers every policy, state and request list. Byte-wise account equality is sound, and an allow verdict implies that the receiver passed the allowlist check. Then the proof uses induction on the list. The model wrote 23 versions, and 17 Lean runs failed. The attempt reached its one-hour limit before the model said DONE, and the check here is on the last version that it wrote.
SlidingTwiceCap-deepseek-v4.1-flash-2: The model had no proof after an hour and five versions. The last version is a probe of the cases of step, with the proof still sorry. Three replies ended at the 16,000-token limit, and the gateway still cut two requests at 600 s. So we lowered the limit to 10,000 tokens for the third attempt.
NonceCountsPayments-deepseek-v4.1-flash-: The model had no proof after 68 minutes and fifteen versions. The last file is a 19-line probe (an allowed step's nonce is not at its maximum). It does not compile and has no Solution.proof. The gateway cut one request at 600 s.
SlidingTwiceCap-deepseek-v4.1-flash-3: The model wrote nothing: three of its seven requests got no response (one after 514 s, two at 600 s). By then the model wrote 15 to 23 tokens/s, as the attempt that ran beside it measured. At that rate a 10,000-token thought can miss the 10 minutes. From the fourth attempt on, the request limit follows the measured rate.
